data.name: Odessa
data.gender_notes: Odessa is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'odos', meaning way or road. In ancient Greece, this name was given to a goddess of the hearth, home, and childbirth. In the Bible, it refers to the port city on the Black Sea. The name Odessa has been used as a feminine given name since the 19th century. The name Odessa carries the meaning “Lady, Wife, or Wealthy” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Odessa usually hope their child will grow to embody lady, wife, or wealthy and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Odessa total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.
data.cultural_impact: Odessa as a Christian name is associated with ancient Greek mythology and the Biblical city in Ukraine. Its origins in Greek mythology give it a rich historical and cultural background, while its association with the Biblical city steeped in history and tradition adds a sense of depth and meaning to the name.
data.spiritual_significance: Odessa as a Christian name holds spiritual significance as a reminder of the goddess of home and childbirth. It invokes images of nurturing, care, and protection, instilling a sense of comfort and warmth. The name is also a reminder of the journey, or the way, that life takes us on, reflecting the Greek root 'odos', meaning way or road. Ultimately, it is a name that inspires a sense of home, comfort, and the journey of life.
